# Fixtures

`simple.pdf` is a hand-written one-page PDF generated by this repository setup.
It contains the text `RAIT simple PDF fixture` and no external copyrighted source.

`two-pages.pdf` is a hand-written two-page PDF generated by this repository setup.
Page 1 contains `First page of the RAIT fixture` and page 2 contains
`Second page of the RAIT fixture`. It has no external copyrighted source.

## Generated document fixtures

`sample.docx`, `sample.epub`, `sample.html`, and `sample.pptx` are generated
from `sample.md` by running `tests/fixtures/make-documents.sh` with pandoc
3.9. The markdown source contains only text written for this repository:
headings, a bold paragraph, a bullet list with a nested sub-item, a numbered
list, and a small pipe table. There is no external copyrighted source.

`edge.docx` is generated by `tests/fixtures/make-edge-docx.py`, a stdlib-only
Python script that hand-writes a minimal WordprocessingML package (zipfile
plus written-by-hand XML parts). It exercises document-parsing edge cases
that pandoc alone does not produce from markdown: a title style paragraph, a
localized heading style id, a paragraph split across multiple runs, a table
with vertically merged cells, a horizontally spanned cell, a multi-paragraph
cell, and a nested table, bullet and decimal list numbering with a nested
bullet level, a duplicated mc:AlternateContent textbox (a DrawingML choice
and a VML fallback that both hold the same text, as real Word documents do),
and tracked changes (an inserted run and a deleted run). All of the text
content in this fixture was written for this repository and has no external
copyrighted source.

Both scripts are run from the repository root as
`./tests/fixtures/make-documents.sh` and write their outputs back into
`tests/fixtures/`. `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` and `TZ` are set before invoking
pandoc, and `make-edge-docx.py` writes its zip entries with fixed timestamps
and sorted names, so re-running the scripts produces byte-for-byte
reproducible output aside from pandoc's own non-deterministic internals
(such as generated ids), if any.

## Generated table fixtures

`sample.csv`, `sample.tsv`, `sample.xlsx`, `sample.parquet`, `sample-zstd.parquet`,
and `edge.csv` are generated by `tests/fixtures/make-tables.sh`, which runs
`tests/fixtures/make-tables.py` with `uv run --no-project --with openpyxl
--with pyarrow`, so no global Python packages need to be installed. All of
the data in these files is fixed synthetic data written for this repository
(a small 25 row sales table with region, quarter, revenue, units, active,
zip, day, and note columns, plus a short edge case table), with no external
source.

`sample.csv` and `sample.tsv` hold the same 25 rows in comma and tab
separated form. `sample.xlsx` holds the same rows on a sheet named `Sales`
using real numeric, boolean, text, and date cell types, plus a second sheet
named `Notes` with two key/value rows. `sample.parquet` and
`sample-zstd.parquet` hold the same rows with an explicit Arrow schema,
compressed with snappy and zstd respectively. `edge.csv` is a small,
hand-written CSV that exercises parser edge cases: a UTF-8 byte order mark,
duplicate and empty header names, a header containing a comma, a quoted
field containing a comma, a quoted field containing an embedded newline,
escaped quotes inside a field, and a ragged row with fewer fields than the
header.

`make-tables.py` fixes the xlsx workbook's `created` and `modified`
document properties to 2026-01-01, and rewrites the saved xlsx archive's
zip entry timestamps and `docProps/core.xml` `modified` value afterward,
because openpyxl's writer otherwise stamps `modified` with the current time
on every save. Re-running `make-tables.sh` produces byte-for-byte
reproducible output for all of the table fixtures.

## Generated PDF table fixture

`tables.pdf` is generated from `tables.tex` by running
`tests/fixtures/make-pdf-tables.sh`, which builds it with `pdflatex` in a
temporary directory and copies only the resulting PDF back into
`tests/fixtures/`. All of the text is original, written for this repository
about storage systems, with no external source. The document is four pages:

- Page 1, "Quarterly Results", has a short paragraph, a borderless
  `booktabs` table (region, Q1, Q2, growth percentage) and a closing
  paragraph. It tests detection of a table with no ruling except the
  `booktabs` top, mid and bottom rules and no vertical rules at all.
- Page 2, "Storage Engines", has a fully ruled table (`\hline` between
  every row, `|` vertical rules between every column) comparing RocksDB,
  LevelDB and WiredTiger, with a `p{5cm}` description column whose RocksDB
  and WiredTiger cells wrap onto multiple lines. It tests detection of a
  conventional grid-ruled table with wrapped cell text.
- Page 3, "Design Notes", is two-column prose with no table at all: about
  350 words split across several paragraphs on the storage engine write
  path, in-memory buffering, reads and background compaction. It has no
  table and exists only to check that a table detector does not report a
  false positive on justified two-column body text.
- Page 4, "Latency Breakdown", has a `booktabs` table with a spanning
  header (`Latency (us)` spans a `p50`/`p99` sub-header via
  `\multicolumn` and `\cmidrule`) followed by a separate small two-column
  key/value `booktabs` table of configuration settings. It tests detection
  of a table with a multi-row spanning header and of a second, much
  smaller table on the same page.

The script exports `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH=0` and `FORCE_SOURCE_DATE=1`, and the
document's preamble sets `\pdfinfoomitdate=1`, `\pdftrailerid{}` and
`\pdfsuppressptexinfo=-1`, so `tables.pdf` has no embedded build date or
trailer ID and re-running `make-pdf-tables.sh` produces a byte-for-byte
identical PDF.

## Generated image fixtures

`photo.jpg`, `text.png`, `alpha.png`, `tiny.gif`, and `tiny.webp` are
generated by `tests/fixtures/make-images.sh`, which runs
`tests/fixtures/make-images.py` with `uv run --no-project --with pillow
--with piexif`, so no global Python packages need to be installed. All
pixel content is synthetic (solid colors, a two-color gradient, and
hand-drawn text), with no external source, and no embedded timestamps
other than the fixed EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` on `photo.jpg`, so
re-running `make-images.sh` produces byte-for-byte identical files.

`photo.jpg` is 60x40 pixels as stored, left half solid red and right
half solid blue, saved at JPEG quality 90. It carries EXIF `Make`
"RAIT", `Model` "Fixture Cam", `DateTimeOriginal`
"2026:01:02 03:04:05", and `Orientation` 6 (rotate 90 degrees
clockwise to display upright, at which point the image is 40 wide by
60 tall). It exercises EXIF metadata and orientation handling.

`text.png` is a 700x220 white RGB image with two lines of black text,
"RAIT OCR TEST" and "Invoice 4217", rendered with a 48pt sans font. It
is meant for OCR testing; running tesseract against it recovers both
lines of text.

`alpha.png` is a 32x16 RGBA image, fully transparent on the left half
and opaque green (0,255,0,255) on the right half. It exercises alpha
channel handling.

`tiny.gif` is an 8x8 palette-based GIF, red on the left half and blue
on the right half. It exercises indexed color / palette image
handling.

`tiny.webp` is a 10x6 lossless WebP image, solid color (0,128,255). It
exercises WebP format support.

## Generated archive fixtures

The files under `tests/fixtures/archives/` are generated by
`tests/fixtures/archives/make-archives.sh`, which runs
`tests/fixtures/archives/make-archives.py` with the system `python3`, plus
the `zstd` CLI and `uv run --no-project --with py7zr` for the formats
python's standard library cannot write. All archive contents are synthetic
text written for this repository, with no external source. Every archive
uses fixed metadata: mtime 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z (epoch 1767225600), uid and
gid 0, and mode 0644 for files and 0755 for directories, so re-running
`make-archives.sh` produces byte-for-byte identical output.

Most archives hold the same small sample tree, in this fixed order:
`docs/`, `docs/readme.txt`, `docs/notes.md`, `data/`, `data/numbers.csv`,
`empty/` (an empty directory). `sample.zip`, `sample.tar`, `sample.tar.gz`
(and its copy `sample.tgz`), `sample.tar.xz`, `sample.tar.bz2`,
`sample.tar.zst`, and `sample.7z` all hold this tree, compressed with
deflate, none, gzip, xz, bzip2, zstd, and LZMA2 respectively.

`sample.7z` is built with py7zr instead of bsdtar's `--format 7zip` writer:
bsdtar's 7z writer turned out to embed the staged files' and directories'
inode numbers in its compressed output, so two otherwise-identical staging
directories (same content, same mtimes, different inodes) produced
different archives. py7zr does not have that problem and was verified
byte-for-byte reproducible across repeated runs with freshly recreated
staging directories.

`sample.a` is a Unix `ar` archive (the common BSD/GNU format, magic
`!<arch>\n`, 60 byte member headers) holding only `readme.txt` and
`numbers.csv` as flat entries (`ar` has no directories), written directly
by hand in `make-archives.py` for exact byte control. Apple's own `ar -p`
does not extract from it (it looks up member names without the trailing
`/` that this format's short names carry), but `tar -tvf` / `tar -xvf`
(libarchive) read and extract it correctly.

`readme.txt.gz`, `readme.txt.zst`, `readme.txt.xz`, and `readme.txt.bz2`
each hold just the bytes of `docs/readme.txt` ("RAIT archive fixture\n
second line\n"), compressed with gzip, zstd, xz, and bzip2, for testing
single-file compressed formats.

`evil.zip` and `evil.tar` are intentionally hostile archives for testing
safe extraction against path traversal and other unsafe entries. Both
raw-encode a `../escape.txt` entry and an entry with a leading `/`
(`/abs.txt`); `evil.zip` additionally has an entry with an internal
`nested/../../` component and a symlink entry (`link`) pointing at
`/etc/passwd`; `evil.tar` additionally has a symlink (`link`) to
`/etc/passwd`, a hardlink (`hard`) to `../outside.txt`, and a character
device entry (`dev`, major 1 minor 3). None of these entries should ever
be written outside of an intended extraction directory, and the device and
link entries should never be created verbatim, by code under test.
